evidence.field: 形義通解; 甲骨、金文、簡帛字例
evidence.text: The dictionary describes the oracle-bone and bronze graph as two hands facing the same direction, sometimes joined, suggesting friendliness; it also explicitly says 又 functions as a phonetic. It reports oracle-bone uses as a personal name and as 侑 in a sacrificial context. Bronze examples use 友 for friend/friendly and for associates or officials, citing 趞曹鼎, 牆盤 and 令方彝. It reports Mawangdui Laozi A 友弱勝強 corresponding to B 柔弱勝強. The page gives no absolute dates for these specific witnesses; these contextual attestations do not by themselves establish a continuous semantic chain.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：友

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: The record lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript and small-seal forms. Its explanation says the early graph uses two 又 (hands) as semantic elements, with small seal arranging the 又 forms vertically. It supports the two-hands analysis but does not establish that cooperation was the historically intended concept. The character-specific page states that it reserves all rights; it is cited as evidence, not proposed as an image source.
evidence.title: 漢字「友」：字形演變

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary reports the received Shuowen account: 同志為友。从二又。相交友也. Its organized definitions include friend, make friends, love, and assist or cooperate; that ordering is not evidence of chronological development.
evidence.title: A00470 友 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: Exact local rows: 又, Mandarin yòu, Middle Chinese hjuwH, Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷəʔ-s, gloss ‘also, in addition’; 友, Mandarin yǒu, Middle Chinese hjuwX, Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷəʔ, gloss ‘friend’. These are Baxter–Sagart 2014 readings in one reconstruction system. Their similar Old Chinese forms make a phonetic relation plausible, while the final differs; the rows alone do not prove the component function. The accessible external PDF search attempt returned 502, so these local readings are not represented as externally verified page content.

gaps: The separate historical dictionarial evidence supplies Zhengzhang and Baxter–Sagart reconstructions in the dossier, but this run externally verified neither pair directly; the local Baxter–Sagart rows were checked as provided and retain that system's notation. The role of one versus both 又 components remains unresolved.

Earliest reported oracle-bone uses are personal-name and 侑 sacrificial contexts; the available sources do not establish that ‘friend’ is the earliest attested sense. The cited witnesses were not independently inspected as primary artifact records, and absolute dates for each example are not provided.
The stepwise semantic relationship from name or sacrificial 侑 to friend, friendly, associate, or verbal uses is unestablished. Do not derive chronology from the dictionary's sense list.

The Mawangdui 友-for-柔 example is a reported whole-graph loan in a manuscript context, separate from the phonetic role of 又 within the compound graph. No independent phonetic history for the loan pair was verified here.
Unicode Unihan endpoints for U+53CB and U+53C8 were inaccessible, so official click-through records could not be cited despite supplied local kMandarin rows.

The two Commons vector pages were discovered, but file-specific license terms were not verified in accessible page content. No image is selected because the reuse provenance requirement is unmet. No exact Xiaoxuetang character-form record/image URL was retrieved. The character-specific chardb page states All Rights Reserved; it is evidence only. No bulk-reuse terms were verified for repeated dictionary text.

limitations.text: No glyph image is proposed: Commons pages for modern 友 oracle-style and Shuowen seal-style vector redraws were located, but their file-specific reuse terms were not verified. The Xiaoxuetang query page did not return an accessible character-specific image record in the web tool. The chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw graph-evolution page is linked evidence only and states All Rights Reserved.
